question.worked_solution:
The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}3{a}_{i}(4-{b}_{j}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{15}3{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}(4-{b}_{j}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}3{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}(4-{b}_{j}) & =(3{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{12}4-{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}{b}_{j}) \\  & =(3{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{a}_{i})\cdot (4{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}1-{\sum }_{j=1}^{12}{b}_{j}) \\  & =(3\cdot 30)\cdot (4\cdot 12-45) \\  & =(90)\cdot (48-45) \\  & =(90)\cdot (3) \\  & =270\end{aligned}
$$
